findings: F1: AC coverage refs can point to positive cases while claiming negative/boundary coverage.
F2: Three-view reviewer verdicts are not part of the machine contract.
F3: cross_unit_obligations[].handoff_obligation_refs do not resolve to real QA obligations.
F4: special_test_triggers are SOP-only and can be empty when design triggers exist.

environment_snapshot.dirty_worktree_note: The worktree also contains unrelated developer runtime layering changes; this fix touched only test-design contract/gate/test paths plus one worklog correction required by validate_context_contract.py.
environment_snapshot.current_environment_reproduction: All four findings were reproduced as fail-closed mutations in test-test-design-canonical-rules.sh and test-test-design-completion-gate.sh.

issues.title: AC coverage type can be forged by positive cases
issues.symptom: negative_case_refs and boundary_case_refs could point at test_cases[].case_type=positive and still pass validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The validator only checks ref arrays and counts, not referenced case semantics.
hypotheses.evidence: tools/community/canonical_test_case_rules.py:35-99 now contains the missing case_type index and ref-type matcher.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The JSON schema alone should distinguish positive/negative/boundary refs.
hypotheses.evidence: The schema can type arrays of strings but cannot resolve string refs to test_cases[].case_type without semantic validation.

root_cause.cause: AC coverage validation stopped at non-empty ref arrays and relative counts instead of resolving refs to case IDs and comparing their case_type.
root_cause.semantic_trace: validate_canonical_rules.py imports assert_test_cases_contract; assert_test_cases_contract calls _assert_ac_coverage_matrix before semantic handoff.

issues.fix: Added case_id -> case_type indexing, unknown ref detection, and strict positive/negative/boundary ref matching.

red_green.red_probe: coverage-type-mismatch mutation in tests/test-test-design-canonical-rules.sh and tests/test-test-design-completion-gate.sh
red_green.green_evidence: bash tests/test-test-design-canonical-rules.sh PASS; bash tests/test-test-design-completion-gate.sh PASS

issues.title: Three-view reviewer verdicts are not machine-enforced
issues.symptom: Deleting all per-reviewer structures still allowed an aggregate PASS to look valid.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The schema/gate only require aggregate review_conclusion fields.
hypotheses.evidence: shared/skills/test-design/contracts/test-cases.schema.json now requires review_conclusion.reviewer_verdicts; tools/community/canonical_test_case_rules.py:120-165 validates each perspective.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reviewer evidence belongs only in human projection, not canonical JSON.
hypotheses.evidence: shared/skills/test-design/SKILL.md:108 makes reviewer_verdicts[] the canonical merge target consumed before completion.

root_cause.cause: review_conclusion treated aggregate PASS/WARN as sufficient and did not require independent test_quality/product/architecture reviewer verdict rows.
root_cause.semantic_trace: test-design SOP writes reviewer results into test-cases.json.review_conclusion; completion_check.sh invokes assert_test_cases_contract for the same artifact.

issues.fix: Added reviewer_verdicts schema/template fields and semantic checks for required perspectives, duplicate perspectives, FAIL blocking, WARN aggregate alignment, issue_count, review_round, and evidence.

red_green.green_evidence: bash tests/test-test-design-canonical-rules.sh PASS; bash tests/test-test-design-completion-gate.sh PASS

issues.title: cross-unit handoff refs do not validate target existence
issues.symptom: handoff_obligation_refs could contain NOT_A_REAL_QA_OBLIGATION and still pass.

hypotheses.hypothesis: handoff refs are checked as non-empty strings only.
hypotheses.evidence: tools/community/canonical_test_case_semantic_rules.py:65 now builds QA obligation ids; lines 333-337 validate cross-unit refs against that set.

hypotheses.hypothesis: qa_stage values are intended as the cross-unit reference target.
hypotheses.evidence: shared/skills/test-design/projections/test-cases-template.md:121 defines obligation_id as the unique target for cross_unit and special trigger refs.

root_cause.cause: The semantic validator lacked a stable QA obligation identity and therefore could not prove cross-unit refs pointed to real handoff obligations.
root_cause.semantic_trace: assert_test_case_semantics collects qa_handoff_contract[].obligation_id before cross-unit validation, then _assert_cross_unit_row checks handoff_obligation_refs against the collected IDs.

issues.fix: Added qa_handoff_contract[].obligation_id to schema/template/fixture/SOP and validate cross_unit_obligations[].handoff_obligation_refs against those IDs.

red_green.green_evidence: bash tests/test-test-design-canonical-rules.sh PASS; bash tests/test-test-design-completion-gate.sh PASS

issues.title: Special test triggers are SOP-only and can be silently empty
issues.symptom: A design with quality_attributes, data_architecture, and cross_cutting_concerns could pass with special_test_triggers=[] and only positive cases.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The completion gate only checks special_test_triggers is an array.
hypotheses.evidence: shared/skills/test-design/scripts/completion_check.sh:128-134 now checks row shape, and tools/community/canonical_test_case_special_rules.py:39-67 checks required source coverage.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Specialty coverage can be inferred from test case titles.
hypotheses.evidence: tools/community/canonical_test_case_special_rules.py:121-132 derives expected refs from design.json quality/data/cross-cutting sources and requires explicit source_ref coverage.

root_cause.cause: No semantic validator existed for design-triggered specialty coverage, so SOP text did not become a machine-enforced contract.
root_cause.semantic_trace: assert_test_case_semantics calls assert_special_test_triggers before cross-unit validation; each row resolves source_ref through design.json and validates backing refs against case, gap, or QA obligation IDs.

issues.fix: Added a dedicated special trigger validator, schema/template fields, Skill/projection guidance, golden fixture triggers, and gate checks for source_ref, handling, and backing refs.

red_green.green_evidence: bash tests/test-test-design-canonical-rules.sh PASS; bash tests/test-test-design-completion-gate.sh PASS

parallel_dimensions.follow_up: Added cross-unit predecessor/successor refs, obligation_id exposure, reviewer_verdicts mapping, Review Round, and Evidence requirements to SOP/projection/prompts.
Migrated delivery-owner-positive-dispatch fixture, added UNIT source support, and strengthened eval expectations.
Removed golden-fixture rewrites from tests, added orphan-test-case validation, and added TYPED_GAP/gap_refs contract coverage.
Extended special trigger eval coverage to require test_case_refs, qa_handoff_obligation_refs, and gap_refs.
Added a non-blocking TYPED_GAP example in the template and governance assertions that gap_refs resolve to design_gap_report.gaps[].gap_id.

resolved_external_blockers.resolution: Fixed developer gate phase-dir derivation and unit-level test-cases lookup.
Aligned optional failure_contract authoritative-field checks with fixture state and added explicit Task file_range dispatch scope.

fix_four_questions.root_cause: The previous implementation described test-design best practices in SOP/projection but did not consistently turn them into semantic rules, schema fields, gate checks, and RED probes.
fix_four_questions.completeness: The repair spans schema, template, semantic validators, completion gate, Skill SOP, projection, golden fixture, and negative tests for each reported false positive.
fix_four_questions.new_risk: New required canonical fields can reject older test-cases.json artifacts; current golden fixture and standard-chain validator pass, but legacy artifacts outside fixtures may need migration before reuse.
fix_four_questions.test_coverage: Each finding has at least one fail-closed mutation in canonical rules and completion gate tests; reviewer verdicts also cover FAIL and WARN aggregate mismatch.
